proposal.summary: The problem is that IBAN format errors in payment data cause refund transaction failures, leading customers to contact support for status updates [E-02, F-02]. This was established by observing five refund failures due to IBAN format errors [E-02] while response times are well under the SLA, showing delay is not the cause [E-01]. The release provides front‑end IBAN error feedback to users and logs each IBAN‑format failure in the payment database [W-PROVIDE-IBAN-ERROR-FEEDBACK, W-LOG-IBAN-ERRORS-PAYMENT-DB]. The release proceeds because the DEFINE Gate resulted in CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring IBAN‑format validation to VOB‑U‑01 (U‑01) whose blocking scope lies outside the release, so the release moves forward with known limitations [U-01, VOB-U-01]. Known limitations: IBAN‑format validation remains deferred to VOB‑U‑01 (U‑01) and the gate is conditional [U-01, VOB-U-01]; furthermore, it is assumed that IBAN validation cannot prevent all input errors such as transposed digits.
